notes: The Frigate arena is a ship interior: narrow corridors, hatches and several decks connected by stairs. It is the tightest multi-level stage in the game, and it plays like Basement stacked vertically.

This stage exports its prop records as bare hex with no type comments; the extractor now walks them with a schema measured from the raw exports, and the walk closes exactly on the array terminator, so its census is trustworthy.
See mp/_general.json for the cross-arena layer.

nuance.claim: Almost the entire stage is narrow corridor, so engagements are head-on at short range and there is very little flanking available on a single deck.
The ship is second only to Bunker for door density, so almost every metre of movement passes a threshold and there is nowhere that is not a chokepoint.
nuance.because: The arena carries twenty-seven Door records across only two hundred and six pads.

nuance.claim: The usual conversion loadout is packed into one of the smallest stages, so armour and ammunition are never far away and attrition strategies do not work.
nuance.because: Two Armour, sixteen AmmoBox and nine Collectable records across two hundred and six pads.

nuance.claim: Banks of screens break up the few open compartments, giving the only cover the ship offers away from its corridors.
nuance.because: The arena carries six MultiMonitor and two SingleMonitor records.

nuance.claim: Because a deck cannot be flanked along its length, the way around an opponent is to change deck and come back, which makes the stairs the most important geometry on the ship.
Since all vertical movement funnels through a few stairwells, mines there cover the routes everyone must use and are extremely strong.
There is nowhere with enough distance to fire an explosive safely, so those sets mostly kill the person using them.
No sightline on the ship is long enough to reward a precision weapon, so rate of fire decides fights instead.
Footsteps carry between decks, so audio tells you someone is close without telling you whether they are above, below or around the corner.
Most contacts happen at a corner or a hatch at point-blank range, so whoever is already aiming wins regardless of weapon quality.
The stage is small enough that opponents are found quickly, so there is little downtime between fights and reloading has to be done expecting interruption.
nuance.because: Two hundred and six pads, at the smaller end of the arena range.

nuance.claim: One-hit kills in corridors mean the player who moves through a hatch first usually dies, so waiting beats pushing.
A carrier survives by cycling between decks rather than running along one, since pursuers lose the thread at every stairwell.
